affected_boundaries: persisted rebase intent to Git result

observed_behavior: Replay supplied with a persisted intent returned schemaVersion, incrementId and result metadata inside its result; the exact V1 reader rejected the extra fields.
expected_behavior: Replay returns only the defined rebase identity and outcome fields regardless of additional intent metadata on its input.
causal_mechanism: TypeScript permits a structurally wider intent record as RollingFastRebaseIdentity. rebasePreparedRollingIncrement passed that object to rebaseResult, whose object spread copied its runtime metadata into the outcome.

anti_pattern.structural_description: Spreading a structurally typed input across an exact output contract boundary.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Static structural compatibility does not strip extra runtime fields.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: The output contains only fields owned by its exact contract.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Project the three defined identity fields before constructing the replay outcome. Preserve exact reader rejection of unknown fields.

applicability_conditions: A caller supplies a wider persisted intent to the structurally typed replay input.
known_non_matches: The original entry point passed a three-field identity and already produced the defined shape.
confirmation_evidence: The existing entry point tests passed while the new persisted-intent replay and PostgreSQL restart fixture both failed with invalid rebase record fields.
Projecting the identity fields makes both regressions pass: ten component tests and three focused PostgreSQL scenarios, with zero failures or skips.
regression_proofs: tests/rolling-integration.test.ts: prepared rebase records exact inputs before replay and refuses changed candidate state
tests/rolling-campaign-store.integration.test.ts: real PostgreSQL serializes allocation, retains ownership and persists accepted review
